passage:
"You were online at eleven. Who were you talking to?" Trisha asked before Siddharth had even taken off his shoes.
"My brother. About Papa's knee."
"You could have messaged me."
Siddharth felt the old urge to hand her the phone, or to walk straight back out. He did neither.
"Trish, I love you. I'm not hiding anything. But I'm not going to show you my chats every night. It makes me feel watched."
"So you won't show me."
"No. But here's what I will do. I'll message you when I reach the office and before I leave. Every day. Can we try that?"
Silence. "And if I panic anyway?"
"Then tell me you're panicking, and I'll sit with you. I won't disappear."
Trisha let out a long breath. "Okay. Office and leaving."

qa.q: Who was Siddharth talking to at eleven?
qa.a: He was talking to his brother about Papa's knee.

qa.q: What did Siddharth feel when Trisha asked who he was talking to?
qa.a: He felt watched and uncomfortable, pulled either to prove himself by handing over the phone or to walk out.

qa.q: What choice did Siddharth make instead of giving in or pulling away?
qa.a: He stayed warm, set a clear limit about the chats, and offered steady messages twice a day, plus company when she panics.

qa.q: How might Trisha feel about the offer to sit with her if she panics?
qa.a: She may feel relieved that her fear is welcomed rather than punished, which is why she lets out a breath and agrees.

grounding: A man who feels watched by an anxious partner avoids both giving in and withdrawing, pairing warm consistency with a clear limit.

passage: I'm Rehana, and last winter I nearly ended things with Vaibhav without meaning to. He'd ask, "Do you still love me?" three times a day. If I went out with my friends, he'd call twice. I felt like I was always sitting an exam I could fail. So I started replying later and later, just to breathe. That made it worse. He got more frantic, sure I was leaving. One night I finally said, "I'm here. I love you. And I need Thursday evenings to myself, no calls." Then I kept both promises, every single week. It took a while. Now he texts "have fun" on Thursdays, and I come home wanting to tell him everything.

qa.q: How many times a day did Vaibhav ask "Do you still love me?"
qa.a: He asked it three times a day.

qa.q: What did Rehana feel when Vaibhav kept checking, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Rehana felt pressured and tested, like always sitting an exam that could be failed.

qa.q: What went wrong at first, and what fixed it?
qa.a: Replying later and later made Vaibhav more frantic; what helped was saying "I'm here, I love you" alongside a clear Thursday limit, and keeping both every week.

qa.q: How did Rehana's slower replies look from Vaibhav's side?
qa.a: To him they looked like proof that Rehana was leaving, so his fear grew and he became more frantic.

grounding: A partner describes feeling constantly tested, pulling away and deepening the fear, then finding that warm consistency with a clear limit works better.

passage: Urmila's phone buzzed right through the team lunch in Gurugram: "Where are you?" "Who's there?" "Send a pic?" Each time she replied, and each time she felt more like a suspect. By dessert she had switched the phone to silent. At home, her partner Swati was waiting on the sofa, eyes red. "You went quiet. I thought..." Urmila felt the old urge to walk straight to the bedroom and shut the door. Instead she sat down beside her. "I love you. I'm not going anywhere. And I can't send photos from every lunch; it makes me feel watched." She paused. "I'll text once when I get there and once when I leave. That's a promise I can keep." Swati's shoulders loosened, a little.

qa.q: What did Urmila do with her phone by dessert?
qa.a: She switched the phone to silent.

qa.q: How did Urmila feel as the messages kept coming?
qa.a: She felt watched and like a suspect, and was tempted to withdraw by shutting the bedroom door.

qa.q: Why did Urmila's approach at home work better than withdrawing?
qa.a: She stayed close and warm while setting a clear, keepable limit, which reassured Swati without giving in to every demand.

qa.q: What is it like for Swati when Urmila goes quiet at lunch?
qa.a: Swati seems frightened and tearful, reading the silence as a sign of being left.

grounding: Shows a partner who feels watched by an anxious partner and chooses warm consistency with clear limits instead of withdrawing.

passage:
"Nazia, your phone's lit up four times since the samosas came."
"It's Faisal. He wants to know when I'll be home."
"It's six-thirty."
"I know." Nazia turned the phone over. "Every evening it's like an exam. Did I reply fast enough, did I say 'love you' back. Some days I want to hide in the office till nine."
Her elder sister Alka poured more chai. "And if you did hide?"
"He'd panic more. Then I'd feel worse. I do love him, Alka."
"So tell him that. And tell him the limit. Not in the middle of a fight."
"Like, 'I'll call when I leave work, but I won't answer ten texts in a meeting'?"
"Exactly that. Warm, and clear."
Nazia typed slowly, then looked up. "He sent back a heart. Just one."

qa.q: How many times had Nazia's phone lit up since the samosas came?
qa.a: Four times.

qa.q: What does Nazia's wish to hide in the office till nine suggest she feels?
qa.a: She feels pressured and tested, as if every evening were an exam of her love.

qa.q: What advice did Alka give, and why might it help?
qa.a: Tell Faisal the love and the limit calmly, not in a fight, so he gets reassurance and a clear boundary.

qa.q: Why might Faisal react better to the calm message than to Nazia hiding?
qa.a: A warm, clear message reassures him, while hiding would feed his fear of being left and make him check more.

grounding: Illustrates a partner who feels watched and pushed to prove love, and learns warm consistency with a clear limit.

passage: The worst month was March. Suraj would ask, three times a night, "You still love me, right?" and I'd say yes, and it never seemed to land. I started staying late at the office, telling myself I needed the quiet. I'm Deepak, and I'm not proud of that. The later I came home, the more Suraj checked where I was, and the more trapped I felt. One night he said, "You're leaving, I can tell," and I saw that my hiding had built the very thing he feared. So we changed it. I come home by eight and say so warmly. I also said, "I won't answer the same question every hour. Ask me once, and trust the answer." It's slower than I hoped. But it's better.

qa.q: By what time does Deepak now come home?
qa.a: By eight.

qa.q: How did Deepak feel as Suraj checked more and more?
qa.a: Deepak felt trapped and pressured, and stayed late at the office to escape.

qa.q: What went wrong at first, and what helped fix it?
qa.a: Pulling away confirmed Suraj's fear; coming home at a steady time warmly while setting a limit on repeated questions helped.

qa.q: How does Deepak's staying late affect Suraj?
qa.a: It makes Suraj more frightened of being left, so he checks more and finally says, "You're leaving, I can tell."

grounding: Shows a partner who withdraws under pressure, sees it confirm the other's fear, and shifts to warm consistency with clear limits.

passage:
Counsellor's session note, Tanuja and Aparna, week three.
Tanuja said she feels "watched". Aparna asks where she is several times a day and gets upset if a reply takes long. Tanuja admitted she has started leaving her phone in her bag on purpose. Aparna's eyes filled: "That's exactly when I feel you're leaving."
I pointed out the loop gently: the more one asks, the more the other hides, and the hiding feeds the fear.
Tanuja said, "I love her. I just can't prove it every hour." She looked worn out.
What we did next: Tanuja chose what she can keep up warmly: a message when she leaves the office and a call at lunch. She also named a limit: no tracking her location. Aparna agreed to note her worry in a notebook before messaging. We will review in two weeks.

qa.q: What limit did Tanuja name?
qa.a: No tracking her location.

qa.q: How was Tanuja feeling in the session?
qa.a: She felt watched and worn out, loving Aparna but unable to prove it every hour.

qa.q: Why is Tanuja's plan better than giving in or hiding the phone?
qa.a: A message when she leaves office and a call at lunch give warm consistency, while the no-tracking limit protects her, so neither of them feeds the loop.

qa.q: How does Tanuja's hidden phone look from Aparna's side?
qa.a: To Aparna, it is exactly when she feels Tanuja is leaving, so the withdrawal confirms her fear.

grounding: Shows a partner who feels watched and pulls away, and how warm consistency plus a clear limit helps more than giving in or withdrawing.
